Bogotá: aerial view of neighbourhoods, high-rises and roads
Arcaded courtyard with tiled roofs and flowers in Villa de Leyva, Colombia
Villa de Leyva: a flowering garden in a courtyard framed by white arches

After breakfast, explore the area around Villa de Leyva.

The first stop is **Casa Terracota**, a house built entirely of clay. Many of its furnishings and objects are also made of clay or ceramic. Although construction is still unfinished, you can visit the house as a museum.

Next, visit El Infiernito, an archaeological site with stone pillars left by the Muisca people. The Spanish called the site “Little Hell”. Local people used the positions of the pillars and their shadows to determine when to sow crops and used them in harvest rituals.

After lunch, which is **not included in the price**, head to Ráquira. This small town has many craft shops selling pottery, woodwork and metalwork. You can also join optional workshops run by local artisans and shops.

Then return to Bogotá and head to the airport for your flight to Armenia. **The flight is not included in the price.**

We recommend a flight departing Bogotá after **19:00**.

On arrival at Armenia Airport, you will be met and transferred to your hotel.

**Duration:** 10 hours.

**Included:** admission to the sites on the itinerary, a bilingual guide, private transport and a local medical assistance card.
